messages:
maya: quick q — I'm proposing a lightweight 'slice' hint for the reorderer API so callers can express latency vs throughput preference. use-case: mobile clients that need best-effort sub-50ms latency opt out of batching. thoughts?

devon: +1 to giving callers a hint. prefer header so routing happens early. e.g. `x-reorderer-slice: low|balanced|bulk`

maya: yep header is my preference too. body arg is messy for proxies.

akshay: header works but impacts billing/quota. low slices will raise unit costs since they bypass batching. we need explicit mapping to quota units.

chloe: from console POV we should surface per-slice breakdown in tenant reports. new charts: `reorderer.slice.latency_p50/p95` and `billing.slice_units_by_tenant`.

devon: telemetry: tag spans/metrics with `slice=low|balanced|bulk`. keep 100% traces for low during rollout window (2w) to validate latency SLOs.

maya: fallback policy question — if low-latency pool is saturated, should we: 1) transparently downgrade to balanced and set header `x-reorderer-fallback: balanced`, 2) return 429, or 3) route to balanced but mark as billing-exempt?

akshay: customers who choose low might expect strict behavior. I'd prefer option 1 *only* if tenant has `allow_slice_downgrade=true`. otherwise 429 with clear error body.

chloe: console UX: add per-tenant toggle 'allow slice downgrade' and a canary override toggle for ops. show recent fallback events in tenant timeline.

devon: quota model proposal: introduce `slice_units` metric. weight candidates: low -> 3 units, balanced -> 1 unit, bulk -> 0.5 units. billing ledger stores `slice_unit_count` per request. open to adjustments after sim.

maya: routing rules sketch: if header=low -> route to low-latency pool. if pool_full: if tenant.allow_slice_downgrade => route to balanced and set `x-reorderer-fallback: balanced`; else return 429 with body {"error":"low-latency pool exhausted","suggestion":"try balanced or enable downgrade"}

ops-bot: FYI deploy plan suggestion: feature flag `reorderer.slice-route-v1` on canary hosts; emit metric `reorderer.slice.routed_total{slice}` and `reorderer.slice.fallback_total`.

akshay: infra note — low-latency pool needs autoscale + cost alerting. otherwise we'll overspend. also limits per-tenant to prevent noisy-neighbor.

maya: rollout checklist I'm thinking: 1) API header + proto change, 2) telemetry tags + dashboards, 3) billing mapping + ledger field, 4) console toggles (allow_downgrade + slice breakdown), 5) canary with 10% tenants, 6) open opt-in for tenants to test.

chloe: UX copy draft: 'Request slice preference (low, balanced, bulk). Low provides lowest latency at higher cost. Balanced is default.' We'll also show estimated unit cost per slice in the quota meter.

devon: I'll file an RFC and add the proto diff. rough timeline: alpha next week (internal), canary 2 weeks after, full rollout after infra autoscale validation.

maya: adding one acceptance test: simulate fully-saturated low pool -> expect `x-reorderer-fallback` header when tenant allows downgrade, or 429 otherwise.

chloe: I'll mock console tiles and the fallback events panel this afternoon :ok_hand:

maya: thanks — I'll open the RFC + confluence doc with telemetry dashboards and sample queries. pinging @devon when PR is ready.

devon: got it, will review.

maya: small example snippet for docs:
```
Request header: `x-reorderer-slice: low`
Possible response headers: `x-reorderer-fallback: balanced` or none
Error (if not allowed): 429 {"error":"low-latency pool exhausted"}
```

chloe: one more ask — include `slice` label in logs (not just metrics) so support can debug tenant-level fallback incidents faster.

maya: agreed. we'll include `slice` in structured log payload.

akshay: sounds like a plan. watch autoscale cost closely when canary starts.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll open the RFC and PRs.
